standard_prerequisites.name: Knuth equivalence of matchings
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two matchings are Knuth equivalent when one can be obtained from the other by a sequence of elementary Knuth transformations.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Core of a matching
standard_prerequisites.statement: The core is the matching induced on the vertices that are not removed by any reduction process.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the invariant the lemma claims is preserved.

core_obligations: Reduce the hypothesis to a single elementary Knuth transformation: since the two matchings are equivalent there is a sequence of such transformations joining them, and it suffices to show that one step preserves the core (source line 1132).
For a single elementary Knuth transformation, compare the reduction processes of the two matchings and show that the same set of chords is removed, so that the cores coincide (source line 1132).

proof_roadmap.step: Replace Knuth equivalence by one elementary Knuth transformation.
Show that one elementary transformation leaves the removed-chord set, hence the core, unchanged.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled lemma at source lines 1128-1130, the first of the two steps into which the author splits the proof of the theorem that two matchings are Knuth equivalent if and only if they have the same core. It states that two Knuth equivalent matchings have equal cores. The author gave it no label, so its position in the article is part of its identity. The proof (source lines 1131-1133) is short but requires a step that the statement hides: Knuth equivalence is generated by elementary Knuth transformations, so the invariant has to be checked on a single elementary transformation, and that check is done by comparing which chords the reduction process removes before and after the transformation. The statement mentions neither the reduction to one transformation nor the comparison of removed-chord sets.
